chapter_title: The World of Metals and Non-metals

zero_omission_notes.summary: All 118 known elements are broadly categorized into metals and non-metals based on physical and chemical properties. Metals are generally hard, lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous, and excellent conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals are dull, brittle, non-malleable, non-ductile, and poor conductors. Key exceptions include sodium/potassium (soft metals cut with a knife) and mercury (liquid metal at room temp). Metals burn in oxygen forming basic oxides, whereas non-metals form acidic oxides.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Malleability allows materials to be hammered into thin sheets (gold, silver, aluminium). Ductility allows drawing into thin wires (copper, iron). Metallic lustre gives fresh surfaces shiny reflection. Sonority produces ringing sound on striking.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Metal Exceptions
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Sodium and potassium are soft enough to cut with a butter knife. Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 4.2 Chemical Reactions with Oxygen and Water
detailed_sections.full_notes: Magnesium ribbon burns in oxygen with blinding white light to yield Magnesium Oxide (MgO), which dissolves in water forming Mg(OH)2 (turns red litmus blue = Basic). Sulfur burns forming Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), forming sulfurous acid in water (turns blue litmus red = Acidic). Iron rusts in moist air forming brown hydrated iron oxide.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: 118 Elements
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Everything in the universe is constructed from 118 chemical elements cataloged in the periodic table.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: To test materials for malleability by hammering.
procedure_or_steps: Place each sample on an anvil surface.
Strike each sample firmly 3-4 times with a hammer.
Observe whether sample flattens into a sheet or breaks into pieces.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Iron nail and copper wire flatten into thin sheets without breaking. Coal and sulfur lump shatter into fine powder.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Metals possess malleability (flatten under impact), while solid non-metals are brittle.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Draw hammer striking a flattened metal sheet on an anvil block.
diagrams_figures_and_maps.structural_or_conceptual_explanation: Visualizes mechanical deformation characteristic of malleable metals.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The property of a material allowing it to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Aluminium foil for food packaging; gold foil.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The property of a material enabling it to be drawn into thin wires.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: Copper and copper alloy wires in electrical grids.

textbook_exercises.question: Which metal reacts violently with cold water and air and must be stored submerged under kerosene?
textbook_exercises.answer: Sodium (and Potassium). They react vigorously with atmospheric oxygen and water, releasing heat and catching fire.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: Which of the following is a liquid metal at room temperature?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Mercury is the only elemental metal that remains liquid at standard room temperature.

short_answer_questions.question: Explain why copper is extensively used for electrical wiring whereas sulfur is not.
short_answer_questions.answer: Copper is a highly ductile metal with abundant free electrons, making it an excellent conductor of electricity. Sulfur is a non-metal insulator that shatters easily.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Compare the reaction products when magnesium and sulfur burn in oxygen, and explain how litmus paper identifies their oxide nature.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Magnesium burns to form Magnesium Oxide (MgO), which dissolves in water to form Mg(OH)2, turning red litmus blue (Basic Oxide). Sulfur burns to form Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), forming sulfurous acid in water, turning blue litmus red (Acidic Oxide).

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Provide a comprehensive comparison between metals and non-metals covering five physical properties and two chemical reactions.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Physical: 1. Lustre: Metals shiny, non-metals dull. 2. Hardness: Metals hard (except Na, K), non-metals soft/brittle. 3. Malleability: Metals flatten, non-metals break. 4. Ductility: Metals form wires, non-metals cannot. 5. Conductivity: Metals conduct heat/electricity, non-metals insulate. Chemical: 1. Metals + Oxygen -> Basic Oxides. 2. Non-metals + Oxygen -> Acidic Oxides.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: An artisan designing traditional musical instruments requires metallic wires that produce a resonant musical tone when plucked and can withstand high string tension.

qa.question: Which physical properties of metals make them suitable for musical strings?
qa.answer: Sonority (ability to produce a sustained ringing musical sound) and high tensile strength/ductility (ability to be drawn into wires that stretch without snapping).

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Non-metals exist as solids (carbon, sulfur, phosphorus), liquid (bromine), and gases (oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen).
